CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypogonadism follow-up.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old HIV-positive male here for follow-up on testosterone replacement therapy. Patient reports feeling well overall with good improvements in vigor and sleep quality. He is currently on testosterone 1 mL every 10 days (current dose 140 mg, due to inject Thursday or Friday). Baseline testosterone levels were less than 300 and are now greater than 1,500. Patient reports positive improvements in bloodwork. Notable change in lipid panel with triglycerides decreased from 265 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL over 5 months since starting testosterone. Red blood cell count has increased but remains stable. PSA today is 0.6 (was 0.5 last year). Patient inquired about increasing testosterone dose to 175 mg but was counseled against this due to risk of peaks exceeding 1,500, which puts him at higher risk of blood thickness issues requiring cessation of therapy. Patient agrees with not increasing dose. Patient inquired about indole-3-carbinol for estrogen control; doctor noted estradiol was not elevated when previously checked. Patient has been out of cialis recently.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports feeling good with improved vigor and sleeping well. No other concerns noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
HIV positive.

MEDICATIONS
Testosterone 1 mL every 10 days. Finasteride 2.5 mg daily (half of 5 mg tablet). Cialis 5 mg on workout days, 2.5 mg on other days.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works out. Uses Walmart pharmacy. Prefers paper prescriptions. Uses medication calendar to track testosterone injections. States he is taking correct steps to improve his life.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Cardiovascular: heart sounds normal. Pulmonary: lungs clear, no concerns. General: appears well and trim.

RESULTS
PSA: 0.6 (previous 0.5 last year; normal <4). Testosterone: greater than 1,500 at last measurement. Red blood cell count: increased but stable. Triglycerides: 145 mg/dL (decreased from 265 mg/dL). Estradiol: not elevated when previously checked.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hypogonadism: stable on current testosterone dose of 140 mg every 10 days. No dose increase at this time due to risk of elevated peaks and blood thickness concerns. PSA: to be rechecked annually. Estradiol: offered to retest in fall if patient desires, otherwise no additional testing needed. Refill prescriptions for testosterone, finasteride, and cialis in paper form.
